citation: 'Prairie Avenue.' Halftone plate facing p. 199 in Picturesque Chicago and Guide to the World's Fair (Baltimore: R. H. Woodward and Co., 1892); photographer unrecorded. The same negative is printed as 'A Bit of Prairie Avenue' in Flinn's 1891 guide, as 'Looking south on Prairie Avenue from Eighteenth St.' in Flinn (1892 and 1893), and on the Alfred Holzman Company postcard 'Prairie Avenue' postmarked 1908 (Glessner House Museum).
author: unrecorded photographer; R. H. Woodward and Co. (publisher)
describes_date: Dec. 1887 to 1891: after the Glessner house was occupied (Dec. 1887) and before its first printing (Flinn, 1891)

locator: The whole plate: the west walk of Prairie Avenue from 18th Street looking south, the Glessner house's granite wall at the right, the parkway, the roadway and the east side's walk and parkway beyond.
rights_note: Published in the United States in 1891-1893 (the postcard issue by 1908); the Internet Archive marks the 1892 book NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Only arrangement, counts and proportions are read from it here; no asset is derived from the image.

note: The street section at the Glessner corner a dozen to seventeen years before the scene date, from the west walk looking south. From the walk out: a broad pale walk; a grass parkway carrying one file of tall elms standing nearer the curb than the walk, their boles clear to about a third of their height and the crowns meeting high over the walk, at an irregular spacing of very roughly 25-35 ft by the trunks' convergence; a pale stone curb standing proud of a smooth light roadway; a paved crossing over the parkway from the walk to the curb beside the second tree; and across the roadway the east side's parkway with its own file of trees, a lamp post and carriage blocks at the curb.
